title: KV Fidelity Orchestrator: Hybrid quantization + runtime scheduler experiments
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Experiment plan for a lightweight runtime "fidelity orchestrator" that applies hybrid KV quantization and a per-request scheduler to trade accuracy for memory and latency savings. Goal: validate practical INT8/FP8/INT4 strategies for the KV cache that integrate with Redwood's continuous batching and routing without causing customer-visible regressions.

Scope and hypothesis:
- Evaluate three quant modes: calibrated FP8 (block-wise scale), symmetric per-channel INT8, and block-packed INT4 with compensated residuals.
- Hypothesis A: INT8 (per-channel) will deliver ~2–3x KV memory reduction vs FP16 with <2% next-token likelihood degradation when combined with small per-key calibration tables.
- Hypothesis B: FP8 can give near-INT8 memory reduction with better numerical stability for long-range attention but requires per-layer exponent sharing for stable prefix cache behavior.
- Hypothesis C: INT4 gives 4–6x reduction but must be paired with a runtime fidelity switch (per-token or per-key fallback to INT8/FP16) to keep quality regressions acceptable.

Key experiments (separate runs):
1) Calibration-only sweep: per-layer scale vs per-channel scale for FP8/INT8 on 6 models (7B, 13B variants) using representative prompt corpus (chat, code, summarization). Measure LL delta, next-token accuracy, and token-level KL.
2) Hybrid layerwise probe: assign quant modes by layer groups (early, mid, late) and measure degradation profile across token positions (prefix vs continuation).
3) Runtime fidelity scheduler: simulate request mix with continuous batching and KV cache hits; implement policy that demotes cached keys to INT8/INT4 and promotes to higher precision when model logits show low confidence or rare token sequences.
4) Fallback path and latency probe: evaluate overhead of on-the-fly re-expansion to FP16 for top-k victim tokens; measure p50/p95 latency impact under various batching patterns.
5) Memory/throughput microbench: measure GPU peak memory, occupancy, and tokens/sec for each quant mode under steady-state continuous batching (batch sizes from 1 to 128 concurrent streams).

Metrics and success criteria:
- Quality: next-token accuracy drop <=2% for INT8 relative to FP16 baseline; LL delta median <=0.03 nats/token. For INT4, allow up to 8% drop only if fallback keeps high-impact routes within 2%.
- Memory: INT8 should reduce cached KV size by >=2.5x; INT4 target >=4x.
- Latency: remediation/fallback cost must add <=5ms p95 per affected request on A100-80GB baseline.
- Cost: projected per-1M-token GPU cost reduction >=20% for INT8 path at target throughput.
- Safety: no measurable increase in hallucination rate on evaluation prompts (defined as rate of factually incorrect assertions flagged by eval harness).

Datasets and harness:
- Calibration set: 8k short prompts, 2k long-context (>2048 tokens) prompts, and 2k code-heavy prompts drawn from internal eval corpus.
- Regression set: 5k labeled prompts with human scores (clarity/faithfulness).
- Bench runner: existing runtime microbench harness + new adapter to simulate KV hit/miss distribution matching production telemetry (heavy-prefix, sparse-prefix cohorts).

Implementation notes:
- Quantization code will live behind the existing KV encoding interface; aim for the minimal change path: new encoding flavors (fp8_block, int8_pc, int4_packed) and metrics hooks.
- Add runtime counters: per-key quant_mode, promotion_count, demotion_count, fallback_count, and average_reexpansion_latency.
- Use stochastic rounding during calibration sweeps to estimate variance and select per-key scale factors.
- Provide a config knob to enable per-route policies in Redwood Console (e.g., route X: prefer INT8, route Y: prefer FP8).

Resources and hardware:
- Assigned: 4x A100-80GB test nodes + 2x A40-48GB for lower-memory stress tests.
- Runtime team allocation: 1 eng (Arjun) + 1 eng (Maya) + 0.5 SRE for infra; PM (Lila) for evaluation acceptance.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: catastrophic drift for certain token distributions (rare tokens cause breakage). Mitigation: fast per-key fallback to FP16 computed lazily and cached.
- Risk: excessive scheduling overhead when switching quant modes under continuous batching. Mitigation: amortize decision per-batch and attach quant metadata to batch descriptors to avoid per-token branching.

Deliverables:
- Experiment workbook with per-run metrics and plots exported to the eval dashboard.
- PR implementing encoding flavors and runtime counters.
- Recommendation doc with acceptance thresholds and rollout plan (canary -> A/B -> full).

If experimental targets met, next step is to add Console controls for per-route quant policies and an observability card summarizing KV memory savings and quality regressions.
comments: 2026-02-26: Kickoff meeting held. Agreed on calibration dataset and the three quant flavors. Arjun to prototype int8 per-channel encoder; Maya to prototype fp8 block-scheme. Lila to prepare regression prompts.

2026-03-02: Prototype microbench done for INT8 per-channel on 7B model. Observed ~2.6x KV size reduction and median LL delta 0.018 nats/token on short prompts. Latency unchanged for p50, minor p95 tail increase (~3ms).

2026-03-04: Ran FP8 block sweep. FP8 showed better stability on long-context sets (LL delta 0.011) but required per-layer exponent sharing to avoid drift. Created GH draft: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2981.

2026-03-07: INT4 quick probe: memory reduction ~4.8x but LL delta skewed heavily on code prompts; added immediate fallback flow to re-expand suspicious keys. New microbench shows fallback cost ~6ms p95 on A100.

2026-03-10: Decision to proceed with hybrid scheduler experiments. Need to increase calibration corpus with more code and rare-token cases. SRE requested additional A40 node to reproduce lower-memory runs. PM asked for customer-impact matrix for early canary routes.
